name: PersonalRecommendations
description: Builds a per-user taste profile from previously watched movies and series (genres, cast, crew, studios) and shows a "Recommended For You" row on the home screen for every user, kept up to date on a schedule and after playback.
overview: Personalized recommendations based on watch history
changelog: 0.4.5: Finger/touch drag no longer scrolls the recommendations row at all (touch-action: pan-y instead of pan-x) - only the arrow buttons do. After three attempts at fixing the underlying Android black-screen rendering bug from different angles without it being fully resolved, this sidesteps the touch-scroll interaction that triggers it entirely rather than continuing to chase it. 0.4.4: Found the actual cause of the black screen 0.4.2/0.4.3 didn't fully fix: the scroll arrow buttons' visibility was recalculated on every "scroll" event, and each actual visible/hidden flip forced a layout reflow in lockstep with touch-driven momentum scrolling — matching the reported pattern of it happening more reliably after scrolling forward, back, and forward again (each direction change flips a button's visibility). Arrow visibility is now only computed once at render time and on window resize, never during a scroll gesture; an arrow can stay visible past its end, where clicking it is a harmless no-op. 0.4.3: Fixed the black screen from 0.4.2 not actually being the swipe-back gesture on Android — it was a fast fling (fine when scrolling slowly, broke when flicked and released) which is a known rendering issue with CSS scroll-snap on some Android WebView versions. Removed scroll-snap-type/scroll-snap-align from the row; it no longer snaps to card edges, but scrolls reliably at any speed. 0.4.2: Fixed a black screen on mobile when swiping right past the start of the recommendations row — once the row hit its scroll boundary, the browser was interpreting the continued swipe as its own edge-swipe-back navigation gesture instead of stopping at the row. Added overscroll-behavior-x: contain and touch-action: pan-x so the row keeps the gesture instead of passing it to the page. 0.4.1: Poster images now render as real elements with lazy loading and async decoding instead of CSS background-images, matching how native rows load - previously every card's image was requested immediately regardless of visibility, competing for bandwidth and loading slower as a batch. Images now also fade in once loaded instead of popping in abruptly. 0.4.0: Resource-usage pass. Added a single shared gate so the plugin never runs its scoring work on more than one thread at a time, regardless of which of the scheduled task / playback-triggered refresh / API cache-miss warm-up triggered it. Each user's watch data is now fetched once per refresh instead of twice (the candidate list and the taste profile each independently re-fetched it before). The library scan is now reused for a few minutes across nearby triggers instead of re-querying Jellyfin each time. "Refresh automatically after playback" now defaults to off, so recommendations only update on the schedule you set instead of also scattered through the day as people watch things. 0.3.5: Added left/right scroll arrow buttons next to the row heading (hidden automatically when there's nothing to scroll to on that side), matching the native Continue Watching row. 0.3.4: The "see all" overlay grid now centers each row instead of leaving a sparse, left-aligned last row when the item count doesn't evenly fill it. 0.3.3: Fixed a 504 the widget could trigger on GET /Recommendations/{userId} shortly after every restart — the recommendation cache was empty until the scheduled task's interval trigger first fired (up to the configured refresh interval later), so the endpoint fell back to computing live, which is slow enough on a real library to trip a reverse proxy's timeout. The scheduled task now also runs on server startup, and the endpoint itself never blocks on a cache miss: it returns immediately and warms the cache in the background, with the widget retrying shortly after. Removed the widget script's diagnostic console logging added in 0.3.1/0.3.2, now that the root cause is fixed. 0.3.2: Fixed the widget not appearing on a confirmed 10.11.11 build — the home screen's row container is added by React after the home tab itself, and the previous DOM-change detection was too narrow to catch that moment. 0.3.1: Added diagnostic console logging. 0.3.0: Replaced the private playlist with a "Recommended For You" home screen widget (web/app clients) — series now show as themselves instead of their next unwatched episode. Existing pre-0.3.0 playlists are automatically removed on first startup after upgrading. 0.2.1: Non-blocking refresh. 0.2.0: Switched from collections to playlists (superseded by 0.3.0). 0.1.0: Initial release.
